title: Transcript entropy bounded by communication cost
statement:
Fix $n \ge 1$, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party protocol for the disjointness problem on inputs of length $n$, and let $\mu$ be any measure on the hard sample space. Executing $p$ on the input pair generated by a sample produces a syntactic transcript, and we regard this transcript as a random variable on the sample space. Then its Shannon entropy, computed with respect to $\mu$, satisfies
\[
H[\text{transcript}] \;\le\; c(p)\,\log 2,
\]
where $c(p)$ is the communication complexity of $p$, i.e. the worst-case number of bits exchanged.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic disjointness protocol on inputs of length n
μ is an arbitrary measure on the hard sample space
entropy of the transcript random variable is taken with respect to μ
replaced: The transcript entropy is at most the protocol length in bits, for any ambient measure.
